questions.q: What is treated as a single transaction in Apex?
options: Each individual DML statement
One request as a whole — a trigger execution, method call, or Execute Anonymous run
Each sObject record being saved
A full business day of activity
questions.explain: Apex treats one request — such as a trigger invocation or a method call from a button — as a single all-or-nothing transaction.

questions.q: What happens if an unhandled DmlException occurs partway through a request that already inserted other records successfully?
options: Only the failing statement is undone; the earlier successful inserts remain
Nothing is undone; all records remain regardless of the error
The entire transaction is automatically rolled back, including the earlier successful work
The request pauses and waits for manual intervention
questions.explain: An unhandled error causes the platform to roll back everything done during that request, not just the statement that failed.

options: A Boolean indicating whether a checkpoint was created
A Savepoint value representing the database state at that point in the transaction
The number of records modified so far
A new transaction ID
questions.explain: Database.setSavepoint() marks the current database state and returns a Savepoint you can later roll back to.

questions.q: After creating `sp1`, then `sp2`, then calling `Database.rollback(sp1)`, what happens if you later try to use `sp2`?
options: sp2 still works normally
sp2 is automatically upgraded to match sp1
Using sp2 causes a runtime error, because rolling back past it invalidated it
sp2 silently does nothing
questions.explain: Rolling back to an earlier savepoint invalidates any savepoints created after it; using an invalidated savepoint afterward produces a runtime error.

questions.q: Besides sObject record changes, what else does rolling back to a savepoint undo?
options: Nothing else — only field values on records are affected
Record locks taken after the savepoint are released, and queued emails sent since the savepoint are discarded
All Apex class definitions created after the savepoint
The user's session and login state
questions.explain: A rollback also releases locks acquired after the savepoint and discards any emails queued for sending since that point.
